text_nodes.text: Tested on the faces walking out.

The Department of Homeland Security Science and Technology Directorate ran it for Customs and Border Protection at the Progreso International Bridge in Hidalgo County. The bridge director puts the annual walk out at over 1.1 million.
Customs and Border Protection asked in October 2025.
Cameras went up on poles at different heights, so people of different statures would land in frame. Some of the testing ran after dark on lighting the partners brought.
Six were shown. Three came south.
Six companies were demonstrated at the Maryland Test Facility. Three solutions were carried forward for data collection at the bridge.
A replica of the pedestrian exit environment went up at the Maryland Test Facility first, so the vendors could install and assess their prototypes before taking them to the crossing.

Artificial intelligence built a three dimensional model of the capture zone, watched pedestrian movement, and judged whether a face was good enough to match. The account gives no rate for how often it was right.
One lane was provided for saying no.
Signs in English and Spanish told pedestrians that United States citizens could opt out. An opt-out lane was provided. The mandate the test serves applies to travelers who are not citizens.
The way in is counted every month.
101,306 pedestrians entered the United States here in May 2026, the month the partners were at the bridge. No comparable data is collected on the way out.
Eight slots. Three of them filled.
Three verdicts are on the record. Five measurements a reader would need are not. Nothing was removed and none of the five was ever stated.
No room. No window. No date.

The account announces no comment period and no hearing. The nearest dated public room in this record is a different program. Dallas takes a briefing on its police department's Flock plate readers on September 8th, 2026.
